svg.data-what: gastrulation: the two-layered disc (left) becomes three germ layers through the primitive streak (right)

g.data-what: the epiblast: the upper layer of the two-layered disc; all three germ layers of the embryo will come from it
the hypoblast: the lower layer, which lines the yolk sac and will be pushed aside

path.data-what: the amniotic cavity, above the disc, lined by the amnion; it will surround the whole embryo
the yolk sac, below the disc; in humans it holds no yolk but makes the first blood cells

g.data-what: the ectoderm: the epiblast cells that stay on top; skin and nervous system will come from it
the endoderm: epiblast cells that moved down and replaced the hypoblast; the gut and its glands will come from it
the mesoderm: epiblast cells that went through the streak and spread between the two layers; muscle, bone, blood, heart and kidneys will come from it

path.data-what: the primitive streak: a groove along the midline of the epiblast, through which cells dive down to make the mesoderm and endoderm

g.data-what: cells moving through the streak: the first replace the hypoblast as endoderm, the next spread out as mesoderm
